statement: Signature verification resolves the JWS verification method and proves control of the corresponding signing key; it does not by itself authorize the operation.
Historical verification may require DID/key state appropriate to the message's signing context; resolving only current DID state can be insufficient after key rotation.
An attestation endorses a specific RecordsWrite descriptor commitment and does not automatically carry forward to a later Record version.
Authorization to read and possession of decryption material are separate capabilities; both may be required for useful plaintext access.
Encryption key distribution is a lifecycle problem distinct from ciphertext generation and must account for membership changes, rotation, recovery, and future access.
Revoking future authorization or future key delivery cannot erase plaintext or key material already obtained by a former participant.
Current TypeScript Enbox role-audience encryption control uses reserved $encryption/audience and $encryption/delivery records rather than the draft audienceEpoch/audienceKey lifecycle.

Delivered decryption key scope must never exceed the authorized scope of the Permission Grant that justifies the delivery; a grantKey is admissible only when its delivered protocol/protocolPath scope is covered by an active, non-context-scoped Records Read or Write grant whose grantor is the author and whose grantee is the recipient.

Grant-key coverage is directional and not symmetric: a protocolPath-scoped grant does not cover a protocol-scoped delivered key. A read grant without protocolPath covers the whole protocol; a read grant with protocolPath covers only subtree descendants plus local role paths that the scoped subtree's $actions reference with read; a write grant covers only local role paths carrying $keyAgreement, additionally constrained to the grant's subtree when it is protocolPath-scoped.
